subject: Urgent: production tail latency & 502s on private cluster
messages:
From: Sam Wright <sam.wright@halochron.io>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: production tail latency & 502s on private cluster

Hi Marcus/Laura/Marissa,

We just hit a sustained p95 latency regression on our private cluster deployed in our VPC. Starting ~08:45 PT we see p95 jump from ~220ms to ~2.1s and intermittent 502 responses for streaming chat calls. Throughput hasn't increased — traffic is steady — but the tail is killing our SLAs. Attached is the kv cache snapshot and a short trace (support_trace_20280320.zip).

We need this prioritized: this behavior is causing user-facing failures and our Ops team is fielding incident alerts. Please advise immediate mitigations and whether Redwood can push a rollback or config change.

What we observed: 
- p50 stable, p95 elevated across both model variants (gptx-2-8k and gptx-2-16k)
- 502s correlate with high decoder queue depth on a subset of nodes
- Some nodes show sharp KV-cache growth in the attached logs

Can someone confirm if this looks like a runtime kernel regression or a routing/batching misconfiguration? We are on commit rwd-20280302.

Thanks,
Sam Wright
Principal SRE, HaloChron

Attachments: halochron_kv_snapshots_20280320.log, support_trace_20280320.zip

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: Sam Wright <sam.wright@halochron.io>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: production tail latency & 502s on private cluster

Sam — thanks for the heads up and the traces. I'm opening an incident internally and looping in Jonas (SRE) for an immediate triage. Initial asks: can you confirm whether the workload pattern changed (burst of long-context requests) and whether you applied any recent config changes to autoscaling or batching?

Immediate mitigation options we'll consider in parallel:
- Force fallback to the 8k model variant on the affected route (preserve correctness, reduce KV growth)
- Temporarily decrease max_batch_size and enforce stricter batching windows
- Pin node routing to spread tail requests across more GPUs

Jonas — can you take a look at the trace and the KV snapshot and advise the quickest remedial. I will create a customer-facing status note once we have the cause.

I'll update in 30 minutes.

— Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Sam Wright <sam.wright@halochron.io>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: production tail latency & 502s on private cluster

Marcus/Sam — I pulled the trace and the KV snapshot. Quick notes:
- The 502s are correlated with decoder task timeouts on a small set of worker hosts (host-az3-07 and host-az3-09). Those workers show spike in KV-store GC latency and abrupt memory pressure on the llama-kv process.
- The pattern looks like a sudden amplification in KV lookup miss-rate that triggers aggressive async compaction and GC latency; compaction is blocking the decoder threads briefly and causing request timeouts.
- There is a runtime commit (rwd-20280302) that changed eager compaction thresholds for quantized KV. The timing matches.

Immediate ask for HaloChron: can you (Priya/Sam) confirm whether you enabled any additional prefix caching at the application layer? That can increase KV churn.

Short-term mitigations I'm proposing (ranked by speed):
1) Rollback to previous runtime build (rwd-20280215) on the affected pool (fast, requires node restart, short service blip)
2) Apply a hot config override to raise compaction latency threshold to avoid blocking decoders (no binary change)
3) Enable per-request decoder timeouts longer than default while we stabilize (may increase user-visible latency slightly but reduce 502s)

I'll prepare a targeted patch for compaction backoff and a kernel scheduling tweak; ETA for patch build is ~6h. If you can attach the full node metrics (top/ps/meminfo) for those hosts, that will help validate.

— Jonas Weber
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Priya Desai <priya@halochron.io>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: production tail latency & 502s on private cluster

Jonas — we do have a recent change: last night our app team pushed an aggressive prefix-caching layer to improve perceived latency for warm users. We also enabled a slightly higher request concurrency per client. I[0m attach the node snapshots and the engine metrics (halochron_kv_snapshots_20280320.log).

We prefer option (2) if it's low-risk — a config override — but if rollback is the only way to immediately stop 502s we'll take that. We can't tolerate long restarts during our business hours, so please call out expected downtime for each plan.

Priya Desai
Engineering Lead, HaloChron

Attachments: halochron_kv_snapshots_20280320.log

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: exec-team@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 14:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Escalation: HaloChron private cluster SLA risk — exec visibility requested

Team — looping in execs because HaloChron reports production 502s and an SLA risk window. Summary:
- Customer: HaloChron (healthcare workflow vendor) on Redwood Private (VPC) deployment
- Symptom: p95 increased ~10x, intermittent 502s correlated with KV GC spike on subset of nodes
- Likely root cause: runtime compaction threshold change in commit rwd-20280302 combined with customer-side prefix caching that increased KV churn
- Impact: user-facing failures, PagerDuty alerts, potential contractual SLA exposure for Q1 run-rate account (deal DL-45731)

Requesting:
1) CTO/VP Product awareness for potential emergency build rollback or fast hotfix release
2) Approval for a limited maintenance window if rollback is required (we estimate 5–12 minutes per worker for restart; cluster pool has 8 workers of interest)
3) Sales/Customer Success to notify HaloChron Executive sponsor and coordinate communication cadence

I recommend we prioritize a hot-config override (Jonas has a proposed override), then prepare a hotfix if behavior persists. Jonas — please put remediation steps and quick rollback checklists in the incident ticket.

— Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Sam Wright <sam.wright@halochron.io>, Priya Desai <priya@halochron.io>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 15:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: production tail latency & 502s on private cluster

Sam/Priya — thank you for the prompt data. Quick status and plan: 

1) Immediate action (now): applying hot-config override to raise KV compaction latency threshold + increase decoder timeouts by 50% on the affected pool. This is a non-binary change and should take <2 minutes to apply; no node restarts.
2) Near-term (2–6 hours): Jonas will push a targeted patch (hotfix_kernel_patch.diff) that implements compaction backoff and reduces GC stalls; we will run the build through internal canaries and then offer a staged deploy for your pool.
3) Contingency (if behavior continues): rollback to rwd-20280215 on the affected pool with a planned maintenance window — estimate 5–10 mins per node with rolling restarts and preserved capacity. We will coordinate the exact window with Priya.

Owner & comms: 
- Technical owner: Jonas (SRE) — triage and deploy: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
- Customer success: Marissa (CC) — ongoing status updates and exec touchpoints: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
- Exec escalation: Laura (Director CR) coordinating with Marcus and product.

Related tickets: https://rwd.atlassian.net/browse/RWD-7890. We will post nightly progress notes to the shared drive and HubSpot record.

We will update you at 15:40 PT with the hot-config result.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments (planned): hotfix_kernel_patch.diff
